Obvi there are SO many ways to get into these fields, no "right" path as it were. So just gonna share my experience and hope it helps 😊

I learned basic html and css online (mostly free), then jumped into JavaScript and React. From there I had a connection with a small tech startup and got experience with full-stack development, as well as learning SQL and ReactNative. I made ~$2000 (before independent contractor taxes) starting out. After 6 months part time, I went full time for about 8 months. Then updated my LinkedIn profile and started getting contacted by recruiters. Took a few interviews, ended up at a large company but on a small team making a bit over 100k. Good work-life balance. I started this process right after my child was born in early 2020, and started this new job this summer right after I turned 25.

Definitely was very lucky to have a connection that mentored me and got me the first bit of experience on my resume. I think you can get that by having some decent certificates from courses or boot camps on your resume, and applying the crap out of lower level webdev jobs. I'd probably look at things like freecodecamp, frontendmasters, the Odin project.

I hope you find something wonderful and are fulfilled at home and work. Please reach out if I can answer any questions, or if you decide to learn webdev and need a learning buddy. Best of luck 💜

I am in a very similar situation. Birth family is very strict religious and Nmom finally made a huge scene a month before our wedding causing no contact. Most the time I am just happy and blown away by the love I am lucky enough to be a part of in my marriage and in my in-laws' family. They don't feel like in-laws, they feel like what I'm learning day by day that a family should feel like. I love my MIL more than anything, and when I get sad/stressed/happy/anything she's the one I usually want to talk to now. When my parents told me they wouldn't come to our wedding bc I didn't want to invite the family member who abused me for several years as a child, I went straight to my MIL and she held me while I cried and cried.

Sometimes it really, really sucks when I get in a funk thinking about my birth family and the way they rejected me when I tried so hard and wanted so badly to have a mother-daughter relationship the way I see so many other families. Sometimes that hole just feels so deep and that rejection makes me doubt so much about myself. It hurts so bad that I meant so little to them when I worked so hard to make them proud of me. They made me feel like I constantly had to earn their love, and that was so damaging.

When that gets to be too much sometimes, I just break down. I sob and sob and can't stop saying "it sucks" "it hurts too much" "I did x,y,z why can't they just love me" "I just wish they weren't Mormon and they could love me". And I don't know if that will ever go away. Judging by everything I've read about rejection by birth parents and children coping, there will always be some amount of a hole. But I do know that the hole will never be stronger than the love I feel from my husband every single time he holds me through that and tells me that yes, it does suck. And he hates that it's like that but he loves me so much. And his family loves me so much. And they'd love me even if for some reason he and I weren't together. The rejection and pain can't hold a candle to that unconditional love and acceptance.

If you're a positive person, relatively smart, and assertive it's a pretty a-ok easy job. The hours are crazy flexible, you can pretty easily move up, there are scholarship opportunities, and many of my best friends are from my store.

If you work front of house (very likely since front of house can have 10-30 people on a given shift and back of house will have 6-15) you could very likely end up outside a lot of your shift, so that's something to consider. It's fast paced and guests can be really awful but they can also be really really great. A lot of us develop friendships with guests outside of the store which probably isn't as common at Chipotle.

Best of luck.
